question: Under Section 20-10 of the Illinois Real Estate License Act, a person who practices, offers to practice, or holds oneself out to practice as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent without being licensed is subject to a civil penalty payable to the Department in an amount not to exceed how much for each offense?
explanation: Section 20-10(a) provides that unlicensed practice subjects a person to a civil penalty to the Department "in an amount not to exceed $25,000 for each offense as determined by the Department," assessed after a disciplinary-type hearing.

question: Once the Department has imposed a civil penalty for unlicensed practice under Section 20-10, within how many days after the effective date of the order must the penalty be paid?
choice_a: 20 days
choice_b: 30 days
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: 90 days
explanation: Section 20-10(c) states "the civil penalty shall be paid within 60 days after the effective date of the order imposing the civil penalty," and the order constitutes a judgment enforceable in court.

question: According to Section 20-15 of the Act, what is required for conduct to constitute a "violation" of the Illinois Real Estate License Act?
choice_a: A pattern of at least three prohibited acts within a single year
choice_b: The commission of a single act prohibited by the Act, its rules, or a disciplinary order
choice_c: A finding by the Board that the licensee intended to defraud a consumer
choice_d: Two or more separate complaints filed against the same licensee
explanation: Section 20-15 provides that "the commission of a single act prohibited by this Act or prohibited by the rules adopted under this Act or a violation of a disciplinary order issued under this Act constitutes a violation of this Act."

question: Under Section 20-20(a), what is the maximum fine the Department may impose for each violation established among the enumerated grounds for discipline?
explanation: Section 20-20(a) authorizes the Department to "impose a fine not to exceed $25,000 for each violation" upon any licensee, applicant, or person holding oneself out as such, in addition to other disciplinary action.

question: Under Section 20-20(a)(17), how must a licensee acting as broker, escrow agent, or temporary custodian maintain escrow moneys belonging to others?
choice_a: In the firm's general operating account, provided the funds are separately labeled in the ledger
choice_b: In a special account, separate and apart from personal and other business accounts, until the transaction is consummated or terminated
choice_c: In the personal account of whichever licensee negotiated the transaction
choice_d: In an account jointly controlled with the opposing party's broker
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(17) makes it grounds for discipline to fail "to maintain and deposit in a special account, separate and apart from personal and other business accounts, all escrow moneys belonging to others" until the transaction is consummated or terminated, subject to specified exceptions.

question: Under Section 20-20(a)(17), which circumstance permits an escrow account to be interest-bearing rather than noninterest bearing?
choice_a: The broker verbally agrees with one of the principals to seek interest
choice_b: The principals to the transaction specifically require, in writing, that the deposit be placed in an interest-bearing account
choice_c: The escrow period is expected to exceed 90 days
choice_d: The Department grants approval upon the broker's request
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(17) states the account "shall be noninterest bearing, unless ... the principals to the transaction specifically require, in writing, that the deposit be placed in an interest-bearing account" (or payment of interest is otherwise required by law).

question: Under Section 20-20(a)(17)(B), escrow moneys may be deemed abandoned and transferred to the Office of the State Treasurer as unclaimed property only after how much time has elapsed following receipt of a written demand for the moneys from one of the principals?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 90 days
choice_c: 6 months
choice_d: 1 year
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(17)(B)(iii) permits escrow moneys to be deemed abandoned only "if 6 months have elapsed after the receipt of a written demand for the escrow moneys from one of the principals to the transaction or the principal's duly authorized agent," and only absent disbursement or a pending court claim.

question: Under Section 20-20(a)(18), within how many hours of a Department request must a licensee make available all escrow records and related documents maintained in connection with the practice of real estate?
choice_a: 24 hours
choice_b: 48 hours
choice_c: 72 hours
choice_d: 7 days
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(18) lists as grounds for discipline the "failure to make available to the Department all escrow records and related documents maintained in connection with the practice of real estate within 24 hours of a request for those documents by Department personnel."

question: Which of the following is listed as grounds for discipline under Section 20-20(a)(19)?
choice_a: Failing to furnish copies of documents relating to a real estate transaction, upon request, to a party who has executed that document
choice_b: Failing to translate transaction documents into a client's native language
choice_c: Failing to retain transaction documents for at least 10 years
choice_d: Failing to have every listing agreement notarized
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(19) identifies as grounds for discipline "failing to furnish copies upon request of documents relating to a real estate transaction to a party who has executed that document."

question: Section 20-20(a)(22) identifies which act as grounds for discipline?
choice_a: Depositing escrow funds into an interest-bearing account with the principals' written consent
choice_b: Commingling the money or property of others with the licensee's own money or property
choice_c: Maintaining a separate escrow ledger for each open transaction
choice_d: Disbursing escrow funds pursuant to a court order of competent jurisdiction
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(22) lists "commingling the money or property of others with the licensee's own money or property" as an independent ground for discipline, separate from the special-account escrow requirements of paragraph (17).

question: Under Section 20-20(a)(27), a licensee is subject to discipline for failing to provide information requested by the Department, or otherwise respond to that request, within how many days of the request?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 20 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 60 days
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(27) makes it grounds for discipline to fail "to provide information requested by the Department, or otherwise respond to that request, within 30 days of the request."

question: Under Section 20-20(a)(39), which practice regarding escrow moneys owed to a party who is not the licensee's client is grounds for discipline?
choice_a: Releasing the funds to the non-client party without first obtaining a signed receipt
choice_b: Requiring the non-client party to allow the licensee to retain a portion of the escrow moneys for the licensee's commission or expenses as a condition of releasing the funds
choice_c: Placing the non-client's earnest money in an interest-bearing account without first being asked
choice_d: Disbursing the escrow moneys pursuant to a court order
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(39) prohibits "requiring a party to a transaction who is not a client of the licensee to allow the licensee to retain a portion of the escrow moneys for payment of the licensee's commission or expenses as a condition for release of the escrow moneys to that party."

question: Section 20-20(a)(16) makes it grounds for discipline for a licensee to fail to do which of the following?
choice_a: Account for or remit any moneys or documents coming into the licensee's possession that belong to others
choice_b: Disclose dual agency in writing before signing a brokerage agreement
choice_c: Complete continuing education within 30 days after license renewal
choice_d: Post a "for sale" sign within 5 days of taking a listing
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(16) lists as grounds for discipline the "failure to account for or to remit any moneys or documents coming into the licensee's possession that belong to others."

question: Under Section 20-20(a)(46), which failure by a designated managing broker is specifically listed as grounds for discipline?
choice_a: Failure to attend at least one Department-sponsored seminar each year
choice_b: Failure to provide an appropriate written company policy or to perform any of the duties set forth in Section 10-55
choice_c: Failure to personally supervise every property showing conducted by sponsored licensees
choice_d: Failure to maintain a branch office in every county where the firm transacts business
explanation: Section 20-20(a)(46) identifies as grounds for discipline "a designated managing broker's failure to provide an appropriate written company policy or failure to perform any of the duties set forth in Section 10-55."

question: Under Section 20-20.1, a citation issued for failure to complete required continuing education or post-license education hours may carry a penalty not to exceed what amount?
explanation: Section 20-20.1(a) authorizes citations for continuing education or post-license education deficiencies with "the penalty imposed, which shall not exceed $2,000."

question: Under Section 20-20.1(b), a licensee who wishes to dispute a citation must make a written request for a hearing before the Department within how many days after the citation is served?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 20 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 45 days
explanation: Section 20-20.1(b) requires that service of the citation "clearly state that if the cited licensee wishes to dispute the citation, the cited licensee may make a written request, within 30 days after the citation is served, for a hearing before the Department."

question: Under Section 20-20.1(c), payment of a citation fine becomes disciplinary action reportable on the Department's website only once a licensee has previously received how many citations and been assessed how many fines?
choice_a: 1 or more
choice_b: 2 or more
choice_c: 3 or more
choice_d: 5 or more
explanation: Section 20-20.1(c) provides that payment of a citation fine "shall not constitute disciplinary action reportable on the Department's website or elsewhere unless a licensee has previously received 2 or more citations and has been assessed 2 or more fines."

question: Under Section 20-21.1(b), when the Department issues a rule to show cause why a cease and desist order should not be entered, the rule must allow the recipient at least how many days to file an answer?
choice_a: 3 days
choice_b: 7 days
choice_c: 14 days
choice_d: 30 days
explanation: Section 20-21.1(b) provides that the rule to show cause "shall allow at least 7 days from the date of the rule to file an answer to the satisfaction of the Department," after which failure to answer causes a cease and desist order to issue immediately.

question: Under Section 20-22, what is the criminal classification for a first offense of working or holding oneself out as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent without a valid active license, and what does it become on a second or subsequent offense?
choice_a: A petty offense, escalating to a Class B misdemeanor
choice_b: A Class A misdemeanor, escalating to a Class 4 felony
choice_c: A Class 4 felony, escalating to a Class 3 felony
choice_d: A business offense, escalating to a Class A misdemeanor
explanation: Section 20-22 provides that an unlicensed person working or holding oneself out as a managing broker, broker, or residential leasing agent "is guilty of a Class A misdemeanor and, on conviction of a second or subsequent offense, the violator shall be guilty of a Class 4 felony."

question: Under Section 20-23, while information collected during a Department investigation is generally kept confidential, which items are expressly made public record?
choice_a: A formal complaint filed against a licensee by the Department and any order issued by the Department against a licensee or applicant
choice_b: The investigator's preliminary notes and internal memoranda
choice_c: The complainant's identity and personal contact information
choice_d: Settlement discussions that occurred before a formal hearing
explanation: Section 20-23 keeps investigation information confidential but states that "a formal complaint filed against a licensee by the Department or any order issued by the Department against a licensee or applicant shall be a public record, except as otherwise prohibited by law."

question: Under Section 20-25, in addition to the amount already owed, what fee applies when a check delivered to the Department is returned unpaid or a credit/debit card payment is declined?
explanation: Section 20-25 provides that a person whose check is returned unpaid or whose card payment is declined must pay, in addition to the amount already owed, "a fee of $50."

question: Under Section 20-25, if a person fails to submit the required remittance within 30 days after the Department's notification of a returned check or dishonored card fee, what happens?
choice_a: The matter is referred to the Attorney General for a civil penalty action
choice_b: The Department automatically revokes the license or denies the application, without a hearing
choice_c: The Board schedules a hearing within 60 days to consider the delinquency
choice_d: The Department issues a citation not to exceed $2,000
explanation: Section 20-25 states that if, after 30 days from notification, the person has failed to submit the necessary remittance, "the Department shall automatically revoke the license or deny the application, without hearing."

question: Under Section 20-60, how far in advance of the hearing date must the Department notify the person charged, in writing, of the charges and the time and place of the hearing?
choice_a: At least 10 days before the hearing
choice_b: At least 20 days before the hearing
choice_c: At least 30 days before the hearing
choice_d: At least 60 days before the hearing
explanation: Section 20-60 requires the Department, before taking disciplinary action, to notify the person charged (and the designated managing broker and sponsoring broker) in writing of the charges and hearing details "at least 30 days before the date set for the hearing."

question: Under Section 20-60, within how many days after service of the Department's notice must the charged person file a written answer to the charges with the Board, under oath?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 20 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 45 days
explanation: Section 20-60 directs the Department to require the charged person "to file a written answer to the charges with the Board under oath within 20 days after service of the notice," warning that failure to answer may result in default.

question: Under Section 20-115, absent the exception for false or misleading initial license applications, within how many years after the occurrence of an alleged violation must the Department commence disciplinary action?
choice_a: 2 years
choice_b: 3 years
choice_c: 5 years
choice_d: 7 years
explanation: Section 20-115 provides that "no action may be taken by the Department against any person for violation of the terms of this Act or its rules unless the action is commenced within 5 years after the occurrence of the alleged violation," with an exception where an initial license application contained false or misleading information.
